newsitem.title: BULGARIA: IMF reassures Bulgarians over currency board.
newsitem.headline: IMF reassures Bulgarians over currency board.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund on Friday reassured Bulgarians that trade on the country's financial markets would not be affected if a currency board was introduced.
A statement from the IMF resident mission in Sofia said the markets for government securities and forxchange would continue to function normally.
Panickans rushed to convert their savings into hard currency this week, fearing they might lose their deposits and treasury paper investments under a currency board system.
"Under a currency board the Bulgarian public would be able to both buy and sell state securities freely," the statement said.
"In fact, the stability of financial markets under a currency board would likely result in an increase in confidence in the securities market."
It said Bulgarians would also be able to buy and sell foreign exchange freely.
Politicians and bankers are discussing an IMF proposal to introduce a currency board to stabilise the economy and restore confidence in the lev.
Under the scheme, levs in circulation and banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank must be exactly matched with central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves.
Bulgarians have besieged the State Savings Bank, the country's biggest savings institution, withdrawing more than 14 billion levs since last week.
Some 75 percent of SSB deposits are invested in Treasury paper and depositors feared the finance ministry might suspend payments on government securities under a currency board.
